previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right knee and calf pain and swelling, initially concerning for DVT, but imaging revealed a complex fluid collection consistent with a hematoma. She was found to have a supratherapeutic INR of 4.0 on warfarin, leading to a diagnosis of spontaneous hemarthrosis. Arthrocentesis was performed twice, with fluid analysis showing blood but no signs of infection or crystals. Warfarin was held, INR normalized, and symptoms improved. Her pain was managed with acetaminophen, gabapentin, and opioids. Hypertension persisted during admission, likely due to pain, and was managed with losartan and amlodipine. She has a history of kidney transplant with stable function and therapeutic immunosuppressant levels. Hematology recommended holding warfarin due to bleeding risk outweighing clotting risk, with outpatient follow-up planned. She was discharged home with home health services, on adjusted pain and blood pressure medications, and instructions to take folic acid for hyperhomocysteinemia.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with FSGS status post living unrelated donor 
renal transplant (___), prior DVT and PE off anticoagulation, 
HTN, and gout, presenting with fever and GI symptoms, found to 
have Ecoli bacteremia.

# GNR bacteremia:  Patient initially presented to OSH with 
increasing nausea, vomiting, malaise, and was found to be 
febrile to over 103 degrees and was transferred to ___ for 
further management. Initially, cause of fever and leukocytosis 
were unclear but she was broadly covered with vancomycin and 
cefepime. She was transitioned to ceftriaxone once OSH blood 
cultures showed pan-sensitive ecoli. Her urine culture also 
showed pan sensitive ecoli making a urinary tract infection the 
most likely source of bacteremia. She remained hemodynamically 
stable during admission and leukocytosis and temperature 
improved with antibiotics. There was no sign of ortho hardwear 
involvment and transplant was normal on ultrasound. EBV and CMV 
viral loads and serologies were negative. Patient had a PICC 
line placed on ___ and will continue CTX for ___nd 
date ___. Pt is to follow-up with ID transplant as outpatient.

#Diarrhea: Ms. ___ developed diarrhea the day after starting 
antibiotics. There was a concern c.diff given pervious history 
of infection and immunosuppresion. She was started on empiric PO 
vancomycin per ID team. Initial C. diff study was negative and 
given symptoms, ID requested repeat testing which showed 
negative for C. diff. Diarrhea was then likely due to 
antibiotics given the timing. Patient was started on loperamide 
which improved diarrhea. Pt's Cr remained stable with diarrhea. 
ID also recommended sending off bacterial cx on stool specimens 
despite infectious diarrhea was unlikely.

#?RUL opacity: On chest CT, patient with RUL ground glass 
opacities and tree in ___ nodules concerning for infectious 
process. Patient was clinically well without SOB, cough or 
hypoxia. Given pt's immunosuppressed hx, ID recommended testing 
for fungal/parasitic etiologies: Crypto, Blasto, strongyloides, 
histo, coccidio send off with follow-up in ID transplant clinic 
to review serologies.

# Focal sclerosing glomerulonephritis s/p kidney transplant 
___: Initial concern for acute rejection on admission as 
patient had R flank pain and she said noted this current 
presentation felt very similar to previous episode of rejection. 
Her creatinine was initially elevated but normalized with 
hydration. Elevation was most likely secondary to bacteremia and 
decreased intravascular volume. Tacro and sirolimus levels were 
at theraputic goals. However, Urine protein/creatinine ratio 
elevated compared to 1 month ago. With IVF, pt's Cr returned to 
baseline.

#Headache: Patient developed frontal headache, with pain 
radiating up from left side of neck on 2 day of admission.  
Symptoms were concerning as she had no previous history of 
severe headaches or migraines. There was no neck stiffness, 
photophobia, or neurologic deficits noted. Patient had one 
episode of diplopia but resolved on exam even with extreme 
lateral gaze. Symptoms were most consistent with tension type 
headache. No photophobia or neck stiffness, no fevers. These 
symptoms eventually subsided.

# Hypertension: Patient was slightly hypotensive on admission 
and blood pressure normalized with IV fluids. Her home 
metoprolol was intially held and restarted as she remained 
hemodynamically stable. The remainder of her antihypertensives 
were held.

# Gout: continue colchicine daily

# Joint pain:  continue hydrocodone PRN
